oneLiner: Intel is a politically backstopped turnaround showing its first genuine revenue and margin inflection in a decade - but at ~$102 the market pays ~70x forward earnings for a company whose free cash flow is still negative and whose foundry still loses $2B a quarter.
thesis: The P&L has inflected. Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1B grew 25% YoY - the fastest since 2011 - with non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 nearly doubling the ~$0.22 consensus and non-GAAP gross margin up 12.1pts YoY to 41.8%.

18A is real and shipping. Panther Lake (client) reached broad availability in January 2026 and Clearwater Forest Xeon 6+ (288 E-cores) launched June 2026 through Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro - the first hard proof the process roadmap executes.
Foundry losses are narrowing on schedule. Q2 foundry operating loss of $2.1B improved ~$0.3B QoQ on revenue of $5.8B (+31% YoY), with yields cited as improving and inbound interest in 18A-P.
Data center is growing again. DCAI revenue rose 59% YoY to $6.3B as Clearwater Forest and Granite Rapids restore competitiveness against AMD.

Washington and strategic investors underwrite the story. The US government's $8.9B stake (433.3M shares at $20.47, Aug 2025), plus Nvidia's $5B and SoftBank's $2B investments, make failure politically expensive and funding available.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Jul 23): revenue $16.1B, +25% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin at 41.8% (+12.1pts YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.42, a seventh straight beat. GAAP showed an $11.0B net loss, almost entirely a $12.5B non-cash mark-to-market on the 158.7M government Escrowed Shares (carried as a derivative liability that grows as the stock rises). CCG rose 13% to $8.9B, DCAI 59% to $6.3B, and Foundry 31% to $5.8B with the operating loss narrowing to $2.1B. Adjusted FCF was still negative at -$8.4B as capex ramps. The disclosure that matters most: external foundry revenue of just $293M - the $100B+ foundry bet still has no anchor external customer.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue of $15.8-16.8B, non-GAAP EPS $0.38, on ~42% non-GAAP gross margin - continuation, not acceleration. The debate: bulls see a durable turnaround (18A ramping, foundry losses shrinking, margins normalizing); bears see PC/server restocking plus an AI halo Intel doesn't actually monetize, with cost cuts (a further round of layoffs and ~$1B opex reduction in July 2026) doing much of the EPS work while negative FCF absorbs the cash the government and strategic investors put in.
segments: Data Center & AI (DCAI): $6.3B, ~39% of revenue, +59% YoY
Intel Foundry: $5.8B (+31% YoY) but overwhelmingly internal; external foundry revenue $293M (~2% of total)
competitive: AMD keeps taking x86 share in client and server; Panther Lake and Clearwater Forest are Intel's first competitive 18A counterpunch
TSMC remains the process and ecosystem benchmark; Intel Foundry must win external logic business from a standing start ($293M/quarter external)
Nvidia owns AI compute; Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU only begins customer sampling in H2 2026
Nvidia's $5B stake and x86/NVLink co-development turned Intel's biggest overhang into a partial ally
Arm-based competition (Qualcomm PCs, hyperscaler Arm server CPUs) erodes the x86 pool itself
moat: What honestly remains: the x86 installed base and OEM/enterprise relationships, scale as the only US-owned leading-edge logic manufacturer, and an explicit government backstop. The classic process-leadership moat is not restored - 18A closes much of the gap, but TSMC keeps customer trust and ecosystem, and $293M of quarterly external foundry revenue says the new moat is still aspiration, not asset.
risks: Free cash flow is still deeply negative. Adjusted FCF of -$8.4B in Q2 2026 as capex ramps; the equity is valued on hoped-for earnings power, not cash generation.
The multiple ran far ahead of the recovery. ~71x forward earnings at $102.57 - a 5x move off the government's $20.47 entry - versus old-Intel's historical 10-15x.
Foundry still loses ~$2.1B a quarter with no anchor customer. '18A-P inbound interest' is not an Apple/Nvidia/Qualcomm-scale commitment, and 14A economics depend on landing one.
Government entanglement cuts both ways. Escrowed-share mark-to-market whipsaws GAAP results, and a ~10% state shareholder constrains capacity, M&A and China decisions.
AI exposure is thin. DCAI growth is CPU-led; Intel has no material merchant AI accelerator revenue in 2026 while that market exceeds $200B.
Restructuring fatigue. Roughly 40,000 jobs cut in two years, with new cuts in July 2026 - cost-driven beats get harder from here.
catalysts: H2 2026: Crescent Island AI GPU customer sampling begins
Late 2026: Nova Lake desktop launch; Panther Lake holiday-season volume ramp
H2 2026 ongoing: external 18A/18A-P foundry customer announcements - the make-or-break catalyst
Jan 2027 (est.): Q4/FY2026 results with 14A and capex commitments
pricedIn: INTC trades at $102.57 (Aug 12, 2026) with a consensus forward P/E around 71x - extreme versus Intel's own 10-15x history, though inflated by still-depressed EPS; trailing GAAP earnings are negative on the escrowed-share mark-to-market. The price implies the turnaround compounds: foundry reaching ~2027 break-even, DCAI growth persisting, margins recovering toward the high-40s, and eventually an external foundry anchor. The key debate: genuine earnings-power restoration versus a state-sponsored re-rating - seven straight beats and 25% growth against negative FCF, $2.1B quarterly foundry losses, and $293M of external foundry sales.

scenarios.bear: The 25% growth proves to be restocking plus AI-adjacent sentiment; PC/server demand normalizes in 2027, foundry losses plateau without an anchor customer, and 14A spending forces another capital raise or deeper cuts. The ~71x forward multiple compresses violently - a move back toward $50-60 requires nothing worse than estimates stalling.
scenarios.base: Intel keeps beating modestly: Panther Lake and Clearwater Forest ramp, foundry losses grind toward break-even through 2027, and adjusted FCF approaches zero as capex peaks. The stock digests its 5x run, trading sideways-to-up as EPS slowly grows into the multiple.
scenarios.bull: A named, large external 18A-P/14A anchor customer signs, Crescent Island gains real inference traction, and gross margin recovers toward high-40s. Normalized EPS power of $3+ by 2028 comes into view, FCF turns positive, and the re-rating extends rather than reverses.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FCF is deeply negative (-$8.4B in Q2 alone) through the foundry buildout, so cash-flow valuation is meaningless; the reverse DCF on ~71x forward EPS shows how much recovery is already priced.
